GOAL: Build `site/src/components/LiveFerryxDemo.tsx` — a live, interactive embedding of the REAL Ferryx desktop UI inside the landing page hero, then wire it into the page.

STEP 1 — Study before writing:
- Read `ui/src/App.tsx` end-to-end to understand how it wires `useWorkspaceStore` + `useWorkspaceRuntime` + Sidebar/TabBar/TerminalSplitView.

- Read `ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx` to find how BROWSER panes are rendered. In desktop Tauri the browser content is a native child webview drawn OUTSIDE the DOM (React renders only a placeholder/host div). In the landing page there is no native layer, so you MUST render an <iframe> instead.

STEP 2 — Implement `site/src/components/LiveFerryxDemo.tsx`:

- Browser pane rendering: wherever the real code hosts the native webview placeholder, render an equivalent iframe-based host (src = BrowserState url, sized to the pane rect, hidden when not visible) so browser tabs actually display pages. Reuse real types/interfaces; do not fork the pane layout logic — override only the native-surface part.
- Wrap the whole thing in a macOS-style window chrome: traffic-light dots, title "Ferryx", rounded corners, drop shadow — pure presentation divs around the real UI.
- Fixed sensible height (~520-600px) with internal scrolling/resize handled by the real components' fit logic (TerminalSplitView uses @xterm/addon-fit).
- Export default; the component must be resilient: any unexpected runtime error should be caught by an error boundary that renders a static fallback message, never crashing the landing page.

STEP 3 — Style parity:
- Diff `ui/src/index.css` vs `site/src/index.css`. Merge ONLY the missing CSS variables/utility classes the demoed components need into site's index.css (both use Tailwind zinc dark theme; avoid importing both full files — no double Tailwind base).

STEP 4 — Wire into Hero (`site/src/components/Hero.tsx`):
- Replace the existing fake hand-drawn terminal/browser mockup JSX with the live demo: `const LiveFerryxDemo = React.lazy(() => import("./LiveFerryxDemo"))` wrapped in `<Suspense>` with a skeleton placeholder, so the landing bundle stays lean.

- Do not change other sections (Features/Benchmarks/etc.) in this task.
